fields.description:
## Problem
`workflow/steps.py::GATE_POLICIES` (`default`/`strict`/`advisory`) fails a workflow step by
exact string membership of `finding["severity"]` in a fixed list. Research confirmed this
`gate` step is NOT wired into any of the three real production gate workflows (plan-review,
code-review, completion-verification each use their own bespoke `_decide`/`_reconcile` ops
instead) -- `steps.gate` is exercised only by a retained sample workflow
(`workflow/examples/review_skeleton.yaml`) and a schema-round-trip test fixture
(`tests/e2e/fixtures/roundtrip-demo.yaml`), both of which feed it plain, severity-only
findings (a generic finder+verify pass, not `pass3_decide` output) with no `priority`/
`decision` field at all. Migrating `fail_on_severity` to a priority-only check would silently
make the demo/fixture gate never fail (every finding would default to `priority: 0.0`), losing
its illustrative value with no live behavior actually fixed (nothing real depends on this
gate's severity check today).

## Approach
ADD priority-threshold support to `GATE_POLICIES` ALONGSIDE the existing `fail_on_severity`
(expand, not a replacement) so the gate step works correctly for both today's severity-only
inputs (the demo/fixture) and any future caller that supplies `pass3_decide`-shaped findings
carrying `priority`: each policy gains a `priority_threshold: float | None` key
(`None` = never fails on priority, matching `advisory`'s empty `fail_on_severity: []`);
`default`'s threshold reuses `review_kernel.decide.DEFAULT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD` (the same source of
truth `pass3_decide` uses for its own BLOCK decision, avoiding a second hardcoded number);
`strict` uses a lower threshold than `default`. The `gate` step (`steps.py:215-239`) fails a
finding if EITHER its `severity` is in the policy's `fail_on_severity` list (unchanged
behavior) OR its `priority` (when present) is `>= priority_threshold`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each policy in `GATE_POLICIES` gains a `priority_threshold` key (`float` or `None`);
  `fail_on_severity` is NOT removed from any policy.
- [ ] The `default` policy's `priority_threshold` equals
  `review_kernel.decide.DEFAULT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD` (imported, not duplicated as a literal).
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_steps.py` passes unchanged for every existing
  severity-only test case (`test_gate_fails_on_high_severity`,
  `test_gate_strict_fails_on_any_finding`, `test_gate_advisory_never_fails`,
  `test_gate_unknown_policy_falls_back_to_default`) -- proving this is additive, not a
  behavior change for findings that only carry `severity`.
- [ ] A new test proves the additive priority path: a finding with no `severity` key but a
  `priority` at or above `default`'s threshold fails the `default` policy; the same finding
  with `priority` below the threshold does not.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_review_skeleton.py` passes unchanged (the demo workflow
  that actually exercises `steps.gate` end-to-end keeps working exactly as before, since its
  severity-only findings never trigger the new priority path).

## Testing
Tier: in-process unit test against the real `gate` workflow step function. Oracle: the
step's returned pass/fail verdict for a finding carrying `severity` only, `priority` only, or
neither, under each named policy. Contrast case (test-design.md sec.6, config-effect): run a
priority-only finding through `default` and `strict` and assert the outcomes differ where its
priority sits between the two thresholds. Regression check: the existing severity-only test
suite and the `review_skeleton.yaml` end-to-end test both stay green, proving additive-not-
breaking.
